answer: Each tow rope is gauged for wear before the trip, and the rope maker holds the gauge book with the rope, the date and the wear. A delta rope claimed as gauged fails the book: the gauge must have measured it at the nebula of the trip, and a rope never gauged has no wear to report. Forging a year of gaugings means bribing the rope maker, faking ninety gauge entries and paying 8,200, and the summit book is checked against the snapped ropes at the yard, so a rope whose gauge was never entered parts on the towpath.
